title: Combination therapy with Oral Bempedoic Acid to reach LDL-Cholesterol Targets (COBALT) - a real-world secondary prevention setting study
summary:
Patients with an elevated blood level of low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) and cholesterol deposits in the blood vessels have an increased risk of future cardiovascular events (e.g. heart attacks).  According to current  guidelines, an LDL-C target value of < 55 mg/dL is recommended to minimize the risk in these patients.  If this target value is not achieved with the current lipid-lowering medication with a statin and ezetimibe, the current decision of the Federal Committee (G-BA) from December 2022 recommends the additional intake of the active substance bempedoic acid in this situation in order to fall below the LDL-C target value. Bempedoic acid is available as a single substance (Nilemdo®) or can be taken by switching treatment to the combination preparation with bempedoic acid and ezetimibe (Nustendi®). Both drugs mentioned are already approved drugs. 
Only data from routine treatment will be recorded and evaluated as part of the observational study.
The effect of the additional administration of Nilemdo® or Nustendi® is assessed  as the rate of LDL-C measurements < 55 mg/dL within 3 months after treatment onset.
In addition, the absolute and relative reduction of the value is calculated within 3 months after treatment, as well as the calculation of cost-effectiveness as € saved per patient year after addition of bempedoic acid or switching to the fixed-dose combination with ezetimibe compared to PCSK9 inhibitor therapy with bempedoic acid, based on achieving an LDL-C level < 55 mg/dL (very high cardiovascular risk) within 3 months.

interventions.name:
Therapy escalation by adding bempedoic acid (Nilemdo®) or switching to the fixed-dose combination with ezetimibe (Nustendi®).
In this observational study, only data from routine treatment will be recorded and analyzed.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
•	written informed consent was obtained
•	Age 18-90 years
•	LDL-C target under lipid-lowering therapy consisting of a statin and ezetimibe (taken for at least 4 weeks) was not achieved (based on ESC/EAS guideline CV risk category very high risk)
Exclusion criteria:
•	No written informed consent can be obtained (illiteracy or inability to understand the study)
•	Statin-intolerant patients (defined as intolerance to two or more statins at any dose and inability to tolerate a dose escalation of these agents to a maximal weekly dose of 70 mg atorvastatin, 140 mg simvastatin, pravastatin or lovastatin, 35 mg rosuvastatin, 280 mg fluvastatin and attenuation or disappearance of symptoms (i.e. myalgia) upon reduction or discontinuation of the statin)
•	Lipid-lowering therapy includes a PCSK-9 inhibitor and/or bempedoic acid
•	LDL-C goal of < 55 mg/dL is reached on current lipid-lowering therapy (based on ESC/ EAS guideline CV risk category very high risk)
•	Intake of experimental drugs within 30 days prior to screening
•	Patient is team member or contractor of institution where the study is conducted or family member of the principal investigator, subinvestigators
•	Lipid-lowering medication was changed within 4 weeks prior to study inclusion
